source.title: LLM Unlearning via Loss Adjustment with Only Forget Data
source.authors: Yaxuan Wang; Jia-Heng Wei; Chris Liu; Jinlong Pang; Quan Liu; A. Shah; Yujia Bao; Yang Liu; Wei Wei

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning methods with forget-set and retained-capability measures, but does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: Tests unlearning outcomes on Harry Potter, TOFU, and MUSE-News. It does not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation edits, quantization, or prompt-only attacks. Reported benchmark outcomes are not recovery-attack results. Only selected baseline outcomes are recorded; the paper reports many additional methods and metrics.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper proposing FLAT, a forget-data-only loss adjustment. It reports forget-set and utility metrics for FLAT and baselines on Harry Potter, TOFU and MUSE-News. It applies no relearning, activation-edit, quantization or prompt-based recovery attack, so it cannot show whether forgotten knowledge is deleted or merely hidden. FLAT is not claimed to resist recovery attacks, so it is not a version F counter-method either. Its results describe benchmark unlearning performance only, which does not bear on the shallow-unlearning claim or on A's robustness clause.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim FLAT achieves superior or top-two unlearning with minimal utility loss on HP, TOFU and MUSE-News, without retain data or a reference model. They acknowledge poor MUSE privacy-leakage results, shared by all methods, and urge caution with PrivLeak. They do not evaluate recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes FLAT, a forget-data-only loss-adjustment method; it does not reproduce an attack or recovery procedure from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by task, model, and metric. The authors also report that MUSE privacy-leakage results warrant caution because of the time-dependent news data.

fits_no_version.finding: Across HP, TOFU and MUSE, several baseline unlearning methods cut forget-set memorization but with large utility losses. GA on OPT-2.7B HP reaches PPL 1.1e71; GA and NPO on MUSE reach retain KnowMem 0.0. FLAT reports near-original utility. All methods fail MUSE PrivLeak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods trade off forget-set suppression against retained utility, as measured on standard benchmarks without attacks.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are tested. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated outcomes. Its authors caution that the MUSE PrivLeak metric may be confounded by temporal shifts and evaluation-data selection.
record.rows_left_out: Many per-method and per-metric results in Tables 3–5 and 9–14 were not extracted; priority was given to selected GA and WHP outcomes relevant to unlearning and utility. FLAT and other baselines' full results are not reproduced here.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. Only forget-set similarity and utility metrics are reported.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no activation ablation or internal analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks. The Table 11 prompt-length study varies only the evaluation prefix length.
All: FLAT makes no robustness-to-attack claim.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded rows are baseline results from the study's own method-comparison tables. None measures post-unlearning recovery, so none links to a version, and no verdicts are given. WHP is an original-source method here re-run only as a baseline. The reader's T2/tests classification and its limits_scope labels on A are withdrawn.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the study measures unlearning and utility but not post-unlearning recovery.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set memorization measures are low for both methods, but retained-set utility or privacy-related results are not uniformly preserved; rows r7-r14. The study does not test whether attacks subsequently recover knowledge.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Harry Potter, GA on OPT-2.7B and Llama2-7B
reader_labels.reason: The reported utility measures show substantial costs, while the forget-quality-gap values alone do not establish near-chance targeted accuracy; rows r1-r6.
